by_segment: Established local business (15-40 staff; income = yearly turnover in GBP)
Small team business (4-15 staff; income = yearly turnover in GBP)

why_not: I check Google and Trustpilot before I contact anyone, and there's nothing to check here: no UK reviews, one anonymous project in Kuwait and a demo for a made-up plumber. Pay-when-happy is nice, but I'd still be giving up hours to calls and rounds of changes with someone I can't vet.

Pay-when-happy sounds good, but I get these DMs every month and this one is a bloke in Kuwait with no UK clients and a made-up plumber demo. I want it done for me and not to babysit it, and I can't tell yet if he'll still be answering when something breaks at 9am on a Saturday.

I only hire people another owner I know has used, and I've already had a web designer cold-messaging me this month. A freelancer in Kuwait with no UK clients or reviews just isn't someone I'd hand my business's face to, however good the no-upfront-payment bit sounds.

My Fresha page and Instagram already bring the bookings in, and I knocked up the Wix bit myself. Paying nothing upfront is nice, but I'd still be signing up for £43 a month forever plus someone pushing £325 SEO at me, for a problem I don't really feel I've got.

I've already got a Wix page and Fresha takes my bookings, so £655 plus £43 a month is a lot more than the few quid I pay now for something that does the job. Paying only when I'm happy is nice, but it doesn't make the ongoing cost any smaller.

Pay-when-happy is decent, but £655 plus £43 every month is over £1,100 in the first year, and I can knock something up on Wix or get a cheap freelancer for way less. Money's tight and a site isn't top of my list right now.

My Fresha page takes the bookings and Instagram brings people in, so I don't see what a £655 site plus £43 a month gets me that I don't already have. The pay-when-happy bit is nice, but no risk doesn't mean I need it.
